court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Mr. Rishikesh Ramesh Ankam vs Mrs. Sunita Rushikesh Ankam
facts_of_case: The parties have decided to amicably settle the matter. The husband agreed to pay a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- as one-time settlement and full and final settlement on all her claims for maintenance in the past, present, and future.

legal_principles.principle: A consent decree can be set aside by the parties themselves.
legal_principles.held: By consent of both the parties the Decree of Restitution of Conjugal Rights dated 30th January, 2018 passed in Petition No.A-08 of 2016 passed by the Learned Judge, Family Court, Solapur on the Petition for Restitution of Conjugal Rights by Respondent Wife is set aside.

legal_principles.principle: A consent divorce can be granted under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
legal_principles.held: By consent of both the parties Counter Claim of Appellant for divorce filed in Petition No.A-08 of 2016 under Section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, is converted into a Divorce by mutual consent under section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955

outcome.final_order: The parties have agreed to settle the matter amicably. The husband has paid Rs.10,00,000/- as one-time settlement and full and final settlement on all her claims for maintenance.
